bull.b: Retention above 100% shows existing merchants are expanding their use of dLocal, supporting recurring volume growth without relying solely on new customer wins. This deepening share of wallet can reinforce platform relevance and improve the durability of revenue over the next several quarters.

Raised full-year guidance indicates management sees enough underlying demand and execution strength to support substantial expansion. The combination of higher payment volume and gross profit expectations provides a durable growth framework, while anticipated operating leverage could improve earnings conversion.

Very low leverage limits debt-related financial risk and preserves flexibility to fund product development, geographic expansion, or shareholder returns. Strong returns on equity also indicate that the company is generating substantial profitability from its capital base, supporting resilience through changing conditions.

bear.b: The multi-year decline in gross and net margins shows that revenue growth has not translated proportionally into profitability. Persistent compression could reduce the earnings benefit of continued volume expansion and leave results more sensitive to payment mix, pricing, and processing economics.

The recent cash-flow rebound is encouraging, but the prior negative year demonstrates that reported profitability has not always converted consistently into cash. Such volatility can complicate investment planning and shareholder returns, particularly if working-capital or timing effects recur.

Lower take rates can constrain gross profit growth even when payment volume rises rapidly, especially as large merchants scale at lower pricing tiers. Continued mix shifts toward lower-spread transactions would make monetization less favorable and could limit operating leverage.
